narration: The Dragon King's Son: A Dance Against Disease
This is Cheoyongmu. Unified Silla period to present.
on_screen: Title card: Cheoyongmu · South Korea · Unified Silla period to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Originating in the Unified Silla period, Cheoyongmu is the oldest surviving Korean court dance.
It evolved from a solo performance into a five-person dance by the Joseon era.
It was historically used for exorcism rites and royal banquets.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a ritual to drive off evil spirits and smallpox, it was performed at royal banquets and New Year's Eve exorcisms to promote good fortune and tranquility.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by five men who move with stateliness and vigor.
The performance is punctuated by lyrical song recitations and varies in tempo and style.
on_screen: Formation: Five dancers arranged to represent the four cardinal directions and the center.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear costumes in yellow, red, blue, white, and black.
They don light wine-colored masks with white teeth, tin earrings, lead bead necklaces, and black hats decorated with two peony blossoms and seven peaches.
